To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
BCL-2, BAX and TP53 protein expression are independent prognostic markers in superficial uro-thelial bladder carcinoma.

BCL-2 overexpression is related to lower tumor grade and TP53 overexpression to higher tumor grade, BAX lack of expression to reduced overall survival and BCL-2/TP53+/BAX-/BCL-2+/ TP53+/BCL-2-TP53-/BAX+/BAX+/BCL- 2-TP53- phenotypes to increased mortality.
the expression of BCL-2, p53 and Bax is associated with the clinicopathological features of urothelial cell carcinoma and the prognosis of the patients with this disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the prognostic significance of TP53 and BCL-2 expression in bladder carcinoma.
the role of TP53, BAX and BCL-2 proteins as potential prognostic markers in patients with Ta and T1 bladder uro-thelial carcinoma.
the expression of the BCL-2, BAX, and TP53 proteins in superficial uro-thelial bladder cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BAX and pathological stage are independent predictors of progression- and overall survival respectively.
TP53, BAX and BCL-2 expression are not independent predictors of prognosis in Ta/T1 bladder cancer, but BAX expression may have a prognostic value.
BCL-2 expression in urothelial carcinomas may be a marker of poor prognosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TP53 and BCL-2 expressions are associated with clinicopathological characteristics of bladder urothelium carcinoma.
BCL-2 overexpression and BAX loss are related to a more aggressive phenotype in patients with Ta or T1 urothelial carcinomas.
the TP53/BCL-2/BAX pathway might have a prognostic role in patients with superficial urothelium bladder carcinoma.
The main takeaway from our work is that

BCL-2, BAX and TP53 protein expression are associated with clinicopathologic characteristics in superficial uro-thelial carcinoma, and that BCL- and BAX protein expressions are associated with survival.
TP53 overexpression, BCL- 2 and BAX expression are related to the tumor grade and stage, respectively, in superficial bladder urothelium.
BCL-2 expression was associated with reduced mortality, while BAX expression was associated with increased mortality.
